prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Production PBR ALBEDO MICRO-FIBRE SWATCH for thin old straw cord in a realistic historical game asset.
Input images are material/style references only: use the muted grey-beige natural grass colour in the soldier's rolled mat reference and the fine brittle split fibres in the tuft reference. Generate ONE SQUARE texture filling the whole frame, with nothing but fine flattened dry straw micro-fibres.
IMPORTANT: this texture supplies only the FINE LONGITUDINAL FIBRE GRAIN inside rope strands. The rope twist/braiding is already built in the 3D normal map. Therefore DO NOT draw big braids, diagonal plaits, rope bundles, chevrons, overlapping slabs, knots, timber growth rings, bark, bamboo slats or any large geometric forms.
The fine hairline grass fibres run predominantly HORIZONTALLY left-to-right, with faint tiny longitudinal splits, thin light/dark streaks, minute torn flakes and subtly dusty grey weathering. About 120–180 very narrow subtle fibre lines across the vertical height. Overall nearly uniform old straw grey-beige/tan, softly sun-faded, low saturation, natural off-white and grey-brown variation, avoid orange/golden wood colour.
Completely flat texture scan, uniform cross-polarized neutral illumination, low macro contrast, no cast shadows, no highlights, no gradient, no vignette. Edge-to-edge seamless-looking material surface. No visible rope silhouette, no mat, no isolated objects, no text, no logos, no watermark. It must read as rough natural dry plant fibre when wrapped around a 5–8mm straw cord, never as a wood surface.
